summary: Phase 149O.20L.7L.4 -- Attack-Matrix and AST-Guard Narrow Repair Independent Verification. FINAL VERDICT: NOT VERIFIED -- CONTRACT REPAIR INCOMPLETE (also: AST GUARD REPAIR INCOMPLETE). Verification-only phase; independently re-derived 149O.20L.7L.3's F-7L-5 and F-7L-7 claims from live production/contract state, not from 149O.20L.7L.3's own narrative. CONFIRMED CORRECT: rows 33/34/36/37 and the HMIC-REQ-145 closure paragraph each individually match live production state -- core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py's _FROZEN_AUTHORITY_BEARING_FILES independently recounted at exactly 30 entries; derive_contract_versions returns exactly 5 members live; no literal `mandatory_consumption_implementation_independently_verified = False` assignment exists anywhere in hatp_mandatory_cutover.py; the certification validator has exactly one production readiness/cutover caller (hatp_mandatory_cutover.py's _assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root), confirmed by repository-wide grep; HBDC-001's live Version header reads 1.1. Rows 38/39 confirmed byte-identical to their pre-149O.20L.7L.3 state by direct line-for-line diff against the immutable baseline commit a1190b08. HMIC-001 remains v1.4; HMIC-REQ-050's thirty-file enumeration and HMIC-REQ-052's three limbs confirmed byte-unchanged since baseline. implementation_scope_digest recomputed live against the real repository: 65ff8ab06b5cd7feb2505742cfbb112ffd386c5b2cf34c2d7f3446d92afe15b8, matching the expected value exactly and matching an independent recomputation against the pre-149O.20L.7L.3 baseline. src/pcae/core/hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py, scripts/hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py, hatp_mandatory_cutover.py, hatp_mandatory_certification.py, and all three Class-B verifier files hashed byte-identical to the pre-149O.20L.7L.3 baseline. git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- src/pcae/ returns empty. The repaired _pcae_import_targets helper was independently reconstructed (read directly from source, not trusted from any test) and confirmed, by direct testing against the real helper loaded from the live test module (not a reconstruction), to correctly catch every absolute import form: plain Import, aliased Import, single-line ImportFrom, multiline ImportFrom, aliased ImportFrom, multiple-name ImportFrom, and the protected-module-from-symbol form -- with clean negative controls for string literals, tuple members, comments, and docstrings, and a wildcard import correctly flagged as suspicious rather than silently treated as safe. TWO GENUINE GAPS FOUND, NEITHER REPAIRED (verification-only scope): (1) a whole-document fresh scan (independent of 149O.20L.7L.3's own §57.9 scan) found the HMIC-001 contract's own top-of-document Status/Identity preamble (before section '## 0.') still asserts, present tense, 'The current hard-coded `mandatory_consumption_implementation_independently_verified = False` ceiling (`hatp_mandatory_cutover.py:842-853`) is unchanged.' Independently confirmed false: no such literal assignment exists anywhere in that file (superseded by Wave F, Phase 149O.19.5F, the same fact this phase confirmed for row 34), and the cited line range 842-853 no longer even corresponds to that logic -- it is now substrate-readiness-detail and signing_available initialization code, independently read and confirmed unrelated. This is the identical stale-current-claim defect class as pre-repair rows 33/34/36/37, and 149O.20L.7L.3's own §57.9 scan read this exact paragraph and misclassified it 'HISTORICAL AND TRUE IN CONTEXT' -- it is not historical, it is the document's own live status preamble. Per this phase's own governing item 14 ('any remaining same-class false current claim: NOT VERIFIED -- REPAIR INCOMPLETE'), this alone blocks full F-7L-5 closure. (2) _pcae_import_targets's pcae.-prefix filter silently drops every relative import of the producer -- from . import hatp_deployment_binding_admin, from .hatp_deployment_binding_admin import create_deployment_binding, and from ..core import hatp_deployment_binding_admin all produce zero hits, independently confirmed by mutation-testing a disposable copy of a real src/pcae module (src/pcae/core/paths.py) with each form injected, using the actual production/test helper loaded from the live test file (not a reconstruction). This is not purely theoretical: relative imports are a live convention elsewhere under src/pcae (29 instances independently counted, e.g. src/pcae/schema_runtime/registry.py). Separately and independently, a second, broader critical producer-reachability guard in the same 149O.20L.7L test module -- test_admin_script_is_the_only_non_test_caller_of_the_producer_entry_points, which scans all of src/ and scripts/, a broader scope than the repaired src/pcae-only AST guard -- still calls the unrepaired, .names-blind _pcae_imports, not _pcae_import_targets, read directly from that test function's own AST (not trusted from any narrative) and independently confirmed by mutation test: a disposable copy of a real module with a single-line `from pcae.core import hatp_deployment_binding_admin` injected is not caught by this specific assertion. Per this phase's own governing item 44 ('ensure the old helper's blind spot does not still back the critical producer-reachability assertion somewhere else -- this is important') and item 53 ('no critical guard still relies on the blind helper'), F-7L-7 is therefore classified NOT CLOSED. VERDICT SUMMARY: F-7L-1/F-7L-2 remain CLOSED, untouched. F-7L-5: rows 33/34/36/37 and HMIC-REQ-145 individually CLOSED; whole-document-scan component NOT CLOSED (one same-class stale claim remains, in the preamble). F-7L-7: NOT CLOSED (relative-import bypass; second critical guard still backed by the blind helper). 7J section 31: remains NOT CLOSED. No repair performed this phase (verification-only, per scope) -- both gaps recorded as concrete narrow follow-up recommendations for 149O.20L.7L.5, not fixed here. Full raw -m fast_green suite independently re-run on this phase's own working tree: 269 failed, 7536 passed, 5 skipped, 9 errors -- 278 total non-passing node IDs, of the identical thematic character as 149O.20L.7L.3's own already-published raw baseline count of 263 (a small delta consistent with this phase's own documented working-tree-dirty self-check flakiness pattern); a 278-item deselect list derived from this run produces a clean 7536 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped, run twice for stability, identical both times; all visible failures/errors are thematically unrelated pre-existing suites (Class-B full-HBDC readiness contract integration analysis, shell_gate audit-CLI subprocess timeout flake, HMIC v1.2 HBDC bound-contract-identity test-fixture errors), none touching F-7L-5/F-7L-7's scope. The new tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7l_4_attack_matrix_and_ast_guard_independent_verification.py (42 tests, all passing) encodes both the confirmed-correct claims and the two open gaps as durable, re-runnable evidence -- including two tests explicitly designed to flip red (and require updating, not silent pass) if either gap is independently closed by a future phase. No DeploymentBinding producer/admin/verifier source was touched. No Dell access. No RepositoryIdentity, no DeploymentBinding, no election, no CHGR, no certification, no activation. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Recommended next phase: 149O.20L.7L.5, a narrow, same-version, contract-text-and-test-only repair of exactly the two gaps this phase found, followed by its own independent verification, before the 7J finding may close or first-use sequencing architecture may begin.
